2027-02-13.title: First Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-02-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-02-13.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-13.verse: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
theo: On Thursday Paul left us with every mouth silenced: no one is righteous, not even one. Today he opens a door: “But now, apart from law, the righteousness of God has been disclosed, and is attested by the law and the prophets, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe.” The sentence that follows is one of the most important in the New Testament: “since all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a sacrifice of atonement by his blood, effective through faith.” This matters at the end of the first week of the Great Fast. We do not buy God's favour with our fasting. Grace comes first, freely, through the blood of Christ. Our fasting, prayer and almsgiving are our response to that gift, and grace itself makes them fruitful. Whoever forgets this turns the fast into a ledger of achievements; whoever remembers it fasts with gratitude.

The Gospel gives us the prayer that holds the whole Great Fast together: “Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And do not bring us to the time of trial, but rescue us from the evil one.” The Holy Qurbana of our Church opens with this prayer and returns to it before Communion. Each line is a Lenten programme: God's name first, his kingdom before our plans, bread asked for one day at a time by people who are fasting, forgiveness given and received, and rescue in the time of trial, as Jesus himself was tested in the wilderness. Of all the petitions, Jesus comments on only one: “For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” The week that began with the gift left before the altar ends with the same lesson: the forgiven must forgive.
outline: Ask: which line of the Our Father is hardest for you to pray honestly?
All have sinned; grace comes first.
The Lord's Prayer as a Lenten programme.
“And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
live: Pray the Our Father once today very slowly, pausing a full minute on each petition.
Name before God one person you forgive, and go to confession this Saturday if you can.
2027-02-13.prayer: Our Father in heaven, all of us have sinned and fallen short of your glory, and you justify us freely by your grace in Christ Jesus. Let us fast with gratitude and not with pride. Hallow your name in us, bring your kingdom, give us today our daily bread, forgive us as we forgive, and rescue us from the evil one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we pray the Our Father before Communion: forgiven and forgiving, we receive the Bread of life.

quick: All have sinned; we are justified by grace as a gift.
The Our Father is the programme of the Great Fast.
2027-02-13.action: Pray the Our Father slowly, a minute on each line.
2027-02-13.question: Do I fast with gratitude or with pride?

family.explain: Jesus taught his friends a prayer: the Our Father. We call God our Father, we ask him for our bread each day, and we ask him to forgive us, just as we forgive others. Jesus says this is very important: if we forgive, God forgives us.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who finds it hard to forgive.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we pray the Our Father together slowly tonight, and think about each line?”

illus: A catechism teacher in Irinjalakuda asked her class to pray the Our Father aloud, pausing after the words about forgiving others. One boy fell silent at that line. Afterwards he told her he could not say it, because he was angry with his cousin. The next Sunday he came early and whispered: we made up yesterday. Now I can say the whole prayer.

pm.open: Our Father in heaven, we come to you as your children, justified by your grace. Hallowed be your name. Amen.
share: They are now justified by his grace as a gift (Romans 3:24). Do I receive God's love as a gift, or try to earn it?
Give us this day our daily bread (Matthew 6:11). What does fasting teach me about this petition?
If you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). Whom must I forgive?
pm.resp: Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the free gift of God's grace.
For those who carry old wounds and cannot forgive.
For those who have no daily bread.
For those in the time of trial and temptation.
For our group, that we may pray the Our Father with sincere hearts.
pm.close: Father, you justify us freely in your Son. Teach us to pray as he taught us, and to forgive as we have been forgiven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul says that all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus (Romans 3:23–24). Our fasting does not buy God's love. His love comes first.
So we fast with gratitude, not with pride. Our prayer, fasting and almsgiving are our answer to a gift already given, and God's grace makes even that answer possible.

Jesus gives us the prayer of the whole Great Fast: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name (Matthew 6:9). We pray it at the beginning of the Holy Qurbana and again before Communion. In it we ask for daily bread, for forgiveness, and for rescue in the time of trial.

Jesus explains one line only: if you forgive others, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). As this first week of the fast ends, let us forgive from the heart, so that we can pray this prayer honestly. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus taught us to call God our Father! Tonight, pray the Our Father slowly with your family, and think of someone you need to forgive.

intro: Theme: “And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
Grace given freely, the prayer Christ taught, and the forgiveness that the forgiven must give.

concl: The fast begins and ends in grace: God gives first, and we answer with gratitude.
Pray as Jesus taught, and forgive as you have been forgiven.
